research_rationale: EO 10854 (Dwight D. Eisenhower; signed 1959-11-27; 24 FR 9565, published 1959-12-01; F.R. Doc. 59-10140) is one paragraph. Acting under section 1110 of the Federal Aviation Act of 1958 (72 Stat. 800; 49 U.S.C. 1510) and having determined that the action would be in the national interest, it extends the application of that Act, to the extent necessary to permit the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency to accomplish the purposes and objectives of Titles III and XII, to areas of land or water outside the United States and the overlying airspace over or in which the United States, under international treaty, agreement or other lawful arrangement, has appropriate jurisdiction or control. A proviso requires the Administrator to consult the Secretary of State on foreign relations and the Secretary of Defense on national-defense interests before acting, and bars action the Secretary of State finds in conflict with a treaty or inconsistent with foreign relations, or the Secretary of Defense finds inconsistent with national defense. Identity and page check: the held text is the Federal Register text layer for PDF page 7 of the 1959-12-01 issue; the order's heading, text, signature (November 27, 1959) and filing line (F.R. Doc. 59-10140, filed Nov. 30, 1959) all appear on that page between EO 10853 and EO 10855, and the repository's Montfaucon page-check record for EO:10854 (jobs/montfaucon-page-check/output/FRAGMENTS_OFFICIAL.jsonl) records a passed two-reviewer check that the cited page holds the complete order. Inventory: the dossier's single scope ran from the start of the page and covered only the tail of the preceding land order; it is corrected to one scope covering the order's operative text from 'By virtue of the authority' through the end of the proviso. Later events: EO 11326 section 7 (signed 1967-02-13) removed the Ryukyu Islands from the applicability of EO 10854, and EO 11382 section 6(a) (signed 1967-11-28) substituted the Secretary of Transportation for the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency. Neither revokes the order; the clause continues for every other area. The Federal Register disposition notes for EO 10854 list only 'See: EO 11326' and 'Amended by: EO 11382'. The dossier chain also lists EO 11938, EO 12510 and EO 13207, but those orders amend EO 10000 (additional compensation of employees serving outside the United States) and their held texts do not mention EO 10854. Current basis: the U.S. Code prints the order, as amended by EO 11382, as a note under 49 U.S.C. 40120; the statute it rests on survives as 49 U.S.C. 40120(b); 14 CFR parts 71 and 73 still cite it as authority; and the FAA applied it in a 2024 rule.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause. EO 11326 section 7 and EO 11382 section 6(a) contain no savings text for EO 10854 either, and no clause of EO 10854 has ended, so no residual question about ended commands arises.

earlier_end_check: No clause of this single-command order has an end. The order states no term, condition or sunset. The held texts that name EO 10854 by number (EO 11326, EO 11382, the 1989 OFR codification, FAA rules and notices at 31 FR 4348, 64 FR 60337, 65 FR 38723, 66 FR 49818 and 89 FR 14379, 14 CFR parts 71 and 73, and the U.S. Code note) were read for an earlier end. None revokes or supersedes the order. EO 11326 section 7 ends the order's application to the Ryukyu Islands only, and EO 11382 section 6(a) changes the officer named. The statutory authority was not repealed without replacement: the 1994 revision of title 49 restated former section 1110 of the Federal Aviation Act (49 App. U.S.C. 1510) as 49 U.S.C. 40120(b), which in the held text lets the President extend the application of that part outside the United States when an international arrangement gives the United States Government authority and the President decides the extension is in the national interest.
scope_check: One scope: the extension of the Federal Aviation Act to areas outside the United States under United States jurisdiction or control, with its consultation and non-conflict proviso. The proviso conditions the Administrator's action under that extension and is not a separate command. The heading and the signature block are not operative text.
independent_command_check: The consultation and non-conflict proviso modifies the extension and falls or stands with it; no other command exists in the order, so no independent command survives or ends separately. EO 11326 section 7 removes one area (the Ryukyu Islands) from the single command and leaves the command in force elsewhere.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause. EO 11326 section 7 and EO 11382 section 6(a) contain no savings text for EO 10854 either, and no clause of EO 10854 has ended, so no residual question about ended commands arises.

research_rationale: EO 10977 (John F. Kennedy; signed 1961-12-04; 26 FR 11471, published 1961-12-05) establishes the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal. Section 1 establishes it for members of the Armed Forces who after July 1, 1958 (a) participate as members of United States military units in a military operation in which personnel of any military department participate in significant numbers in the opinion of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and (b) encounter foreign armed opposition incident to that participation or are placed where, in the Joint Chiefs' opinion, hostile action by foreign armed forces was imminent. Section 2 sets the design (approved by the Secretary of Defense), the awarding officials (the Secretary of the military department concerned, and, for the Coast Guard, the Secretary named in the order) and uniform regulations by the Secretary of Defense. Section 3 limits the medal to operations for which no other United States campaign medal is approved and to one medal per person with devices for later operations. Section 4 allows posthumous award. The held text is the official Federal Register text layer for PDF page 3 of the 1961-12-05 issue (location confidence high); the six dossier scopes cover sections 1(a), 1(b), 1 (lead-in), 2, 3 and 4, and the authority recital and signature block are not operative text. Later events read from held texts: EO 11382 section 13(3) (signed 1967-11-28) struck 'Secretary of the Treasury' and inserted 'Secretary of Transportation'; EO 13286 section 72 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) struck 'the Secretary of Transportation' in section 2 and inserted 'the Secretary of Homeland Security'. Three later medal orders provide, notwithstanding section 3, that members who qualified for the medal for service in a named theater remain qualified and may take the later medal instead: EO 11231 section 2 (Vietnam Service Medal, signed 1965-07-08), EO 13154 section 2 (Kosovo Campaign Medal, signed 2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (Global War on Terrorism Medals, signed 2003-03-12). None ends the order. The dossier also lists an EO 12977 entry, but the amendment it quotes is section 72 of EO 13286 (68 FR 10619), a queue file mislabelled with the EO 12977 number; EO 13286 is cited instead and no EO 12977 text is relied on. Federal Register disposition notes for EO 10977 list 'Amended by: EO 11382', 'EO 13286' and 'See: EO 13154'; each is reconciled above. The Code (release point 119-121) records at 6 U.S.C. 111 note that section 72 of EO 13286 amended Ex. Ord. No. 10977 and prints no ending statement. The claim rests on the original-plus-bounded-search route: no held instrument or own term ends any clause, and the three bounded searches found no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause and none of its clauses has ended. The later medal orders preserve entitlement already earned under this order ('shall remain qualified'), which confirms that this order's eligibility rule continued to operate after those orders.
earlier_end_check: No clause has an own-terms end: the order states no date, condition or sunset. The held texts naming EO 10977 by number (EO 11231, EO 11382, EO 13154, EO 13286, EO 13289, the 1989 OFR codification, the 1967 Army reference list at FR 1967-08-17 and the Code note at 6 U.S.C. 111) were searched; none revokes or supersedes it. Each later medal order says its members 'shall remain qualified' for this medal and leaves section 3 otherwise in force, and EO 13286 and EO 11382 only change the officer named in section 2.
scope_check: Six scopes: the section 1 lead-in establishing the medal, its two eligibility conditions (a) and (b), section 2 (design, awarding officials, regulations), section 3 (no other campaign medal, one medal per person, devices) and section 4 (posthumous award). The dossier inventory matches the held text; the authority recital and signature are not operative.
independent_command_check: The establishment and eligibility clauses, the award-and-design clause, the limiting clause and the posthumous clause are separate commands and each continues independently. The substitutions of officers in section 2 and the later exceptions to section 3 change who acts and for whom the limit applies; neither ends a clause.
